title: Copilot Studio: discover and use shared plugins from Microsoft's plugin registry
summary: Hold: the data-policy navigation omits steps needed to edit a policy, and the guidance incorrectly treats data policies as a general way to block plugin connectors. The briefing also assumes an approval flow for the new integration that Microsoft has not documented; its roadmap facts match the record.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: A plugin package can be blocked tenant-wide in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block. ... Select Block, and then select Block again to confirm.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package, using the beta API.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: An existing data policy's connector can be blocked at Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Assign connectors > connector > Block.
claims.quote: To edit an existing data policy, select the data policy and select Edit Policy. ... Select Next. The Add an environment page appears. ... Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears. ... Select the three dots
claims.fix: Replace the path in controls[1].ui and the rendered table with 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Next > Next > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block'. The first Next opens Add an environment; the second opens Assign connectors. See https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention.

Copilot Studio data policies govern Power Platform connectors used as agent tools, not Copilot connectors.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention.
